subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a public normal-chat tool-error delivery policy beyond `messages.suppressToolErrors`, and what should happen when a mutating tool fails but the assistant final reply sounds successful?
rationale: Source inspection confirms the UX gap, but choosing success-aware suppression changes public config and failed-side-effect visibility semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the product contract.

options.title: Add explicit opt-in policy
options.body: Define a default-compatible enum such as `all | final | off` where `all` preserves current warnings and hosted/team-chat operators can opt into final-only or off behavior with focused safety tests.

options.title: Keep boolean-only policy
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported all-off escape hatch and close or defer the success-aware enum after documenting that boundary.

options.title: Move policy to channels
options.body: Let channel plugins own warning visibility where chat UX differs, avoiding another global message config key.

recommendation.title: Add explicit opt-in policy
recommendation.body: Define a default-compatible enum such as `all | final | off` where `all` preserves current warnings and hosted/team-chat operators can opt into final-only or off behavior with focused safety tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest inspected history on the current warning-policy path and authored the merged related PR that explicitly kept this broader issue open.
